summary: Pushpendra Kumar is an Indologist who studied under Satyavrat Shastri. He served as a Lecturer in Sanskrit at the University of Delhi (attested 1976) and as Principal at Shri Lal Bahadur Shastri National Sanskrit University.
Puthezhethu Rama Menon worked in Indology and other fields. He served as a judge at the Chief Court of Cochin and was President of the Kerala Sahitya Akademi.
Pyi Phyo Kyaw is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at King's College London by 2014, where Kyaw later served as a postdoctoral research fellow (attested 2017).

Péter-Dániel Szántó works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He earned an MA from Eötvös Loránd University and a PhD from Balliol College, Oxford, under Alexis Sanderson, later holding posts at All Souls College, Oxford, and Eötvös Loránd University.

Qian Lin works in Buddhist studies and Indology, holding degrees from Fudan University, the University of Bristol, and the University of Washington (PhD 2015). Lin studied under Collett Cox, Richard Salomon, Rupert Gethin, and several other teachers.

Qiang Ning is a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology who completed a doctorate under Wu Hung and Irene Winter. Ning has held teaching posts at Michigan, Yale, and San Diego State, and was a Dunhuang Academy researcher.

Qichao Liang was a Sinologist, historian, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Xuehai Tang and under Kang Youwei. He headed the Translation Bureau (~1898), lectured at Current Affairs Academy and Nankai University, and directed the National Library of China.

Qing Duan worked in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. She earned an MA at Peking University and a PhD at the University of Hamburg under Ronald Eric Emmerick, later serving as professor at Peking University (~1987–2022).

Qingying Chen was a scholar of Tibetology, history, and archaeology. Educated at Qinghai University for Nationalities and Minzu University of China under Wang Yao, Chen taught at Qinghai Nationalities University and directed the Historical Research Institute at China Tibetology Research Center.

Qingzhi Zhu is a scholar of linguistics, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. Zhu held posts as a professor at Peking University (attested 2004) and at the Education University of Hong Kong (attested 2010).
Qinni Liu is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts degree at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Kirill Solonin (attested 2009).
Qiwen Xiao is a scholar of Buddhist studies who completed a Master of Arts degree at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Yongdong Shi (attested 2013).
R. Balasubramanian was an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied under Varahur Kalyanasundara Sastri. He served as Director at the University of Madras from circa 1980 to 1990.
R. D. Vadekar was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Shripad Krishna Belvalkar. He served as Professor of Sanskrit and Allied Languages at Fergusson College (attested 1958).

R. Gordon Wasson studied at Columbia and the London School of Economics, contributing to religious studies and Indology. His career included roles in journalism, the American Council of Learned Societies (1951), Guaranty Trust Company, and J.P. Morgan & Co. (1934–1963).
R. H. Tawney was a historian who studied at Rugby School and Balliol College, Oxford. He held academic posts at the University of Glasgow (~1906–1908) and the London School of Economics (~1913–1949).
R. N. Gadre was an Indologist who served as Professor of Sanskrit at Sir Parashurambhau College and at Savitribai Phule Pune University (both attested 1958).
R. P. Paranjpye was a scholar who studied under Vaman Shivram Apte. He served as Vice-Chancellor of Savitribai Phule Pune University (attested 1959).

R. Ramanujachari was a scholar in philosophy and Indology. He served as Professor of Philosophy at Annamalai University (attested 1938–1940) and as editor of the Journal of the Annamalai University (attested 1950).

R. Sathyanarayana was an Indology scholar who earned a master's in chemistry at the University of Mysore (~1947–1949). He taught at Sarada Vilas College (1949–1984) and served as President of the Indian Music Congress.
